title: Protocol for DNA Extraction from Cowpea
author: Aparna Srinivasan

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary environment and reagents before starting the extraction.

substeps.instruction: Heat water bath to 65 °C and pre-warm CTAB buffer in the water bath for 20 minutes (optionally add 1% PVP to CTAB buffer to handle high phenol content).
Heat incubator to 37 °C.
Chill 70% ethanol to 4 °C.
Ensure RNase (10 mg/ml) and proteinase K (20 mg/ml) are prepared.

steps.title: Collect and Grind Tissue
steps.instruction: Collect cowpea leaf tissue and mechanically disrupt it while keeping it frozen.

substeps.instruction: Collect 1 fully expanded leaf from Cowpea plants in a 50ml centrifuge tube containing five sterile glass beads (5mm diameter) and freeze immediately in liquid nitrogen.
Grind tissue using a vortex, ensuring the tissue remains frozen.
Transfer approximately 0.5 mL of ground tissue to a new 2 mL Eppendorf tube containing two 2mm glass beads.
Further beat the tissue in a bead beater for 1 minute in one direction, then 1 minute in the opposite direction.

steps.title: Lysis and Protein Digestion
steps.instruction: Lyse the tissue and digest proteins using CTAB buffer and proteinase K.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 μl of pre-warmed CTAB buffer and 12 μl of proteinase K (20 mg/ml).
Invert tubes gently to mix and incubate in a water bath at 65 °C for 30 min, inverting once every 10 min to homogenize.
Remove tubes from water bath and centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 15 min to clear the lysate.
Transfer 500 μl of cleared lysate to a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: RNA Removal
steps.instruction: Treat the lysate with RNase to remove RNA contamination.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 μl of RNase (10 mg/ml).
Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the aqueous phase from proteins and lipids using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform and vortex well.
Centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 15 min.
Transfer the upper aqueous layer (~350-400 μL) to a new 1.5 ml Ep tube, ensuring the lower layers are not touched.
Repeat the chloroform step if the aqueous phase is not clear.

steps.title: DNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the nucleic acids using isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of isopropanol and mix very gently.
Incubate for a few minutes (up to 30 minutes at room temperature) until white strands of nucleic acid precipitate are observed.
Centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 10 min to pellet the DNA.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: DNA Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet to remove residual salts and solvents.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 μl of 3M Sodium Acetate and 500 μl 70% ethanol, then centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μl 70% Ethanol, centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 5 min, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: DNA Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Dry and resuspend the DNA for analysis and storage.

substeps.instruction: Air-dry the pellet.
Dissolve the pellet in 50 μl TE Buffer.
Place at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Quality Control and Storage
steps.instruction: Verify DNA purity and concentration before long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Run DNA on a 0.8% Agarose gel to check for degradation or RNA contamination (if RNA is present, treat with RNAse A and repeat from the phenol:chloroform step).
Measure concentration and purity using a Nanodrop (A260/A230 ratio of 1.8-2.0 indicates purity; <1.8 indicates carbohydrate or phenol contamination).
Store DNA sample at -80 °C until use.
